title: ordering reconstruction never reproduces the transactions root once a block carries transactions
summary: With a transaction workload running, EVERY ordering block the Rust node tried to reconstruct fell back with `root_mismatch`: 9 of 9 after the cold restart, 10 of 10 across the run. Not one ingredient was missing - `reconstruction is missing a transaction` never logged - so the planner collected the complete transaction set and still computed a different Merkle root than the header announces. That points at ORDER (or an extra/duplicated member), not at availability. The same node reconstructs coinbase-only blocks successfully (6 times in the same run, and 11 in the unfunded run of the previous round), which is why the defect was invisible until the devnet could fund transactions.

measurement.note: this is the fallback-rate measurement spec §12 F5 asks for

where_to_look: ergo-node/src/node/input_blocks/reconstruct.rs::collect_transactions assembles `plan.non_broadcasted ++ mempool(broadcasted_ids) ++ plan.input_chain_txs`. The Scala miner's ordering block is built by CandidateGenerator's collectTxs, whose order is not that concatenation; compute_root is order-sensitive (transactionsRoot over the id list, with witness ids as the second leaf half from header version 2). Compare a failing block's /blocks/{id} transaction id order against the order the planner produces before changing anything.
impact: M2's headline claim - an ordering block assembled from input blocks instead of a BlockTransactions download - does not hold for any block that carries a transaction. The node stays CORRECT (it falls back and downloads, heights and state roots agree throughout), so this is a feature gap, not a consensus break.
gate: assertion 4 of the devnet-matrix smoke FAILS on this.
